items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: I made a special trip out there to see where General Johnson was shot, and the tree where he died when they laid him up against a tree where he died.

ctx.x: And so, we played those cities. We would go out and stay out maybe a week, a week and a half, then come back to Jackson. Then we'd spend a couple, two or three days. Then we would go down to Corinth, Mississippi, which was on the M&O. That was a different route, see. And going into Tupelo, Mississippi; Okolona, Mississippi; into towns like West Point, Mississippi. And, of course, Starkville, Mississippi, and Aberdeen. And then we'd come back to Tupelo, and we'd go back over west to New Albany, Mississippi.

And so, I used to keep a diary of all these cities that we played, see. And I can remember in Corinth -- we played in Corinth, and that was where the Battle of Shiloh was fought on the Tennessee River. And I made a special trip out there to see where General Johnson was shot, and the tree where he died when they laid him up against a tree where he died. And that to me, that was American history, you know, that I wanted to see with my own eyes.
